checks_by_claim.source_location: Definition 3.2 PDF p.10; Theorem 3.6 p.17; dy0 convention p.5 and self-adjoint martingale scope p.9
checks_by_claim.verification: Let X be the finite fair simple random walk started at 1 and absorbed at 0, let y=-X, x_N=0 and z_N=1. For every positive scale all upper-crossing projections R_n are I, so test (i) is 0<=0. Every squared increment, including dy0^2=1, is at most 1, so test (ii) holds for every allowed projection. Finite horizon gives bounded self-adjoint variables and all required Lp membership; there is no nonnegativity or y0=0 hypothesis excluding y.

Reflection gives P(X_N=j)=2j/(N+1) P(S_(N+1)=j), hence E X_N^4=E|S_(N+1)|^5/(N+1). Jensen gives ||y_N||4>=(N+1)^(3/8). At N=2^17-1 this exceeds 80: raising the comparison to the eighth power reduces to 2^19>5^8. The printed p=4 constant is exactly 48/sqrt(1-(5/4)^-2)=80. This is an analytic exact comparison, not a numerical approximation.

checks_by_claim.claim: Core dependence, opposing evidence and bounded repair
checks_by_claim.source_location: PDF pp.17–19, especially the 'Symmetrically' transition to (3.29)
checks_by_claim.verification: The negative estimate is not justified by the original one-sided assumptions. For the reversed martingale X at scale 1, R0=0 and test (i) has left side at least 1 while its right side is zero; sign symmetry is not automatic. Adding tests for both signs permits the checked one-sided trace/projection arguments to be applied twice in the finite-dimensional tracial setting and gives the stated norm constant.
checks_by_claim.severity_reason: The false result is explicitly a main theorem and the missing estimate is required for its full absolute-value bound. Repair availability does not lower its Major severity.
checks_by_claim.limit: No general unbounded semifinite repair is certified. Strong testing conditions and the square-function application are sign invariant, so this counterexample is not asserted to invalidate every application.
